# Cloud Print Service (CPS): integration and deployment guide for agents

> One file with what an AI agent needs to integrate a business system with CPS, or to deploy it. The authoritative API contract is the OpenAPI spec served by every CPS server at `/openapi.yaml` (source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kucial/cloud-print-service/main/server/internal/httpapi/openapi.yaml). When this file and the spec disagree, the spec wins.

## 1. What CPS is (and is not)

- A print gateway on the warehouse LAN. Business systems own the content (they render ZPL, or produce a PDF/PNG); CPS owns fleet visibility and safe dispatch.
- It does not lay out documents or templates. Send it a finished label or document.
- Components:
  - `cps`: the server. HTTP API, operator panel at `/ui/`, per-printer queues, status polling, document conversion, SQLite store (`cps.db`).
  - `cpsctl`: admin CLI (tokens, agents, printers, diagnostics). Env: `CPSCTL_URL`, `CPSCTL_ADMIN_KEY`.
  - `cps-agent`: runs on a PC or ASUS router that has USB printers; makes them reachable by the server.
  - `vprint`: virtual printer for tests (real ZPL/ESC/POS/IPP/PJL sockets, renders labels to PNG, fault injection).

## 2. Auth

- Every request: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Two roles: `client` (business systems: print, read status, own jobs) and `admin` (everything, including tokens, agents, discovery, previews).
- Admin bootstrap keys live in the server config (`api_keys`). Business systems should get issued tokens: `cpsctl token issue --client-id wms --ttl 365d` (secret shown once; stored hashed; `cpsctl token rotate|revoke <token-id>`).
- Jobs are scoped to the calling client. Another client's `job_id` returns 404.

## 3. Choosing a printer

`GET /api/v1/printers/status` returns the whole fleet in one call (`?ids=a,b,c` to narrow). Per printer:

- `printer_id`, `name`, `site`, `driver`, `kind`, `formats`, `enabled`
- `usable`: true when enabled, online and not in an error or consumable-out state. This is the field to branch on.
- `queue_depth`
- `status.state`: `idle|printing|busy|media_low|media_out|ribbon_out|head_error|error|offline|disabled|unknown`; `status.detail`, `status.observed_at`, `status.stale`

Other reads: `GET /api/v1/printers` (`?site=&usable=`), `GET /api/v1/printers/{printer_id}`, `GET /api/v1/printers/{printer_id}/jobs`.

By default a job for a printer that is not usable is accepted and waits in its queue. With `reject_when_not_usable: true` in the server config, submission fails with 409 `printer_not_usable` instead.

## 4. Submitting a job

`POST /api/v1/jobs` (JSON):

| field | required | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `printer_id` | yes | |
| `external_id` | yes | your business document id; the idempotency key (or send header `Idempotency-Key`) |
| `zpl` | one of | ZPL as text |
| `payload_base64` | one of | any format, base64 |
| `format` | no | `zpl` (default), `escpos`, `pdf`, `png`, `jpeg`, `pcl`, `postscript`, `pwg`, `urf`, `escpr` |
| `copies` | no | 1..`max_copies` (default limit 1000). ZPL: applied as `^PQ`; IPP: job attribute; others: sent that many times |
| `page_copies` | no | ZPL only: per-label copy counts, e.g. `[4, 1]` |
| `priority` | no | `normal` (default) or `high` |
| `biz_ref`, `meta` | no | free text and string map, returned on reads |

Responses: `202` queued; `200` replay (same client + `external_id` + same payload: returns the original job, `replayed: true`); `409 idempotency_conflict` (same `external_id`, different payload or copies).

```bash
curl -X POST "$CPS/api/v1/jobs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"printer_id":"wh1-pack-01","external_id":"SO-10042-label","zpl":"^XA^FO50,50^A0N,50,50^FDHello^FS^XZ"}'
# → 202 {"job_id":"…","state":"queued","printer_id":"wh1-pack-01","external_id":"SO-10042-label","replayed":false,"links":{"self":"/api/v1/jobs/…"}}
```

PDF/PNG/JPEG are converted for printers that do not take them directly (raster for label, receipt and inkjet printers, PCL/PostScript for JetDirect lasers). A format that cannot reach the printer returns 422 `format_not_supported`.

Variants:
- `POST /api/v1/jobs/raw?printer_id=…&external_id=…&format=pdf`: the document as the request body, no base64. The format may also come from `Content-Type` (`application/pdf`, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`).
- `POST /api/v1/jobs/batch`: several jobs, each accepted or rejected on its own.

Payload limit: `max_payload_bytes`, 32 MB by default.

## 5. Job lifecycle

```
queued → sending → printed        printer confirmed it
                 → sent_unknown   bytes reached the printer, no confirmation
                 → failed         did not print (error before any byte was sent, or the printer reported the job failed)
queued → cancelled                POST /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/cancel, only before sending
```

Rules an integration must follow:

1. Retrying the same request with the same `external_id` is always safe; it never prints twice.
2. `failed`: safe to resubmit (a new `external_id`, or fix the cause first). `last_error` and `status_message` say why.
3. `sent_unknown`: do not resubmit automatically. CPS cannot tell "printed, ack lost" from "did not print". Surface it to a person; after they look at the printer, `POST /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/resolve` with `{"resolution":"printed"}` or `{"resolution":"failed"}`.
4. `printed` with `status_message` "Sent; the printer cannot confirm printing": the printer has no status channel (e.g. Epson ESC/P-R inkjets); all bytes were delivered and the printer stayed reachable.

Read state: `GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}` (fields include `state`, `state_detail`, `status_message`, `attempts`, `last_error`, `created_at`, `sent_at`, `finished_at`). Bulk: `GET /api/v1/jobs/status`. List: `GET /api/v1/jobs?printer_id=&state=&external_id=&limit=&cursor=`.

Live updates (optional; polling is enough): `GET /api/v1/events?topics=printer.status,job.state` is a Server-Sent Events stream with `Authorization` header (browser `EventSource` cannot send it; use `fetch` and read the stream).

## 6. Errors

Envelope: `{"error":{"code":"…","reason":"…","message":"…","details":{…}}}`. Branch on `code`, and on `reason` for 422.

| HTTP | code | meaning / action |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `unauthorized` | missing or bad token |
| 403 | `forbidden` | admin route with a client token |
| 404 | `printer_not_found`, `job_not_found` | |
| 409 | `idempotency_conflict` | same `external_id`, different payload: use a new id only if it is really a new document |
| 409 | `printer_disabled` | an operator disabled the printer |
| 409 | `printer_not_usable` | only with `reject_when_not_usable`; pick another printer |
| 422 | `invalid_request` + `reason` | `missing_payload`, `duplicate_payload`, `invalid_base64`, `missing_printer_id`, `missing_external_id`, `invalid_copies`, `copies_conflict`, `invalid_format`, `format_not_supported`, `document_unreadable`, `pdf_conversion_unavailable`, `payload_too_large`, … |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | per-client token bucket; back off |
| 503 | `queue_full` | backpressure; honour `Retry-After` |

## 7. Printer drivers

| printer | `driver` | port | status | prints directly |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Zebra / ZPL label | `zebra9100` | 9100 | `~HS` | ZPL |
| ESC/POS receipt (Epson TM, Xprinter) | `escpos9100` | 9100 | DLE EOT | ESC/POS |
| office printer with IPP | `ipp` | 631 | IPP printer and job state | what the printer reports (PDF, JPEG, URF, PWG…) |
| office printer on JetDirect | `pdl9100` | 9100 | PJL | PCL, PostScript |
| Epson inkjet without IPP (EcoTank L-series) | `escpr9100` | 9100 | reachability only | ESC/P-R (A4, 360 dpi) |
| any of the above on USB | via `cps-agent` | agent dials 19100+ | as above | as above |

Not supported: host-based printers that need the maker's PC driver (Canon CAPT LBP lasers, GDI-only models).

## 8. Deploying the server

Needs: a Linux host on the printers' LAN, and Docker or nothing else (a single binary). Releases: https://github.com/kucial/cloud-print-service/releases (tags `v*`).

```json
{
  "addr": ":8080",
  "api_keys": { "<openssl rand -hex 24>": { "client_id": "ops", "role": "admin" } },
  "printers": [
    { "printer_id": "wh1-pack-01", "name": "Packing station 1", "site": "wh1",
      "driver": "zebra9100", "host": "192.168.10.21", "port": 9100, "enabled": true }
  ],
  "discovery": { "enabled": true, "site": "wh1" }
}
```

```bash
chmod 644 config.json      # the container runs as uid 10001
docker run -d --name cps --restart unless-stopped --network host \
  -v "$PWD/config.json:/etc/cps/config.json:ro" -v cps-data:/var/lib/cps \
  ghcr.io/kucial/cloud-print-service:latest      # pin a version (e.g. :0.1.0) in production
curl http://localhost:8080/healthz      # 200
alias cpsctl='docker exec -e CPSCTL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080 -e CPSCTL_ADMIN_KEY=<admin-key> cps cpsctl'
```

- Without Docker: download `cps-<version>-<os>-<arch>` (linux/darwin amd64+arm64, windows amd64) from the release; it holds `cps`, `cpsctl` and `config.example.json`. Run `./cps -config config.json`. Install `poppler-utils` (and fonts) for PDF conversion; the image includes them. Latest version: `V=$(basename "$(curl -sLo /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/kucial/cloud-print-service/releases/latest)")`, then `https://github.com/kucial/cloud-print-service/releases/download/$V/cps-$V-linux-amd64.tar.gz`. Building from source (`go build ./server/cmd/cps`) needs Go 1.26+.
- Config lookup: `-config <path>`, then `$CPS_CONFIG`, then `./config.json`. Data: `$CPS_DATA_PATH` or `data_path`, default `cps.db`. `store_driver: memory` keeps nothing (tests only).
- `--network host` is only needed for mDNS discovery; otherwise `-p 8080:8080`.
- HTTPS: put a reverse proxy in front; it must not buffer `/api/v1/events` (Caddy `flush_interval -1`, nginx `proxy_buffering off`).
- Network: clients → server 8080; server → printers 9100/631; server → agents 19100+; agents → server 8080; mDNS 5353/udp.

USB printers: download `cps-agent-<version>-<os>-<arch>` (Windows zip, Linux tar.gz) or the ASUS router packages (`cpsagent-<version>.tar.gz` for koolshare, `cps-agent-<version>-asuswrt.tar.gz`) from the release. On the server `cpsctl agent enroll --id pc7 --site wh1 --ttl 24h`, or the panel's Agents → Enroll agent (one-time token); on the PC `CPS_AGENT_SERVER=http://<server>:8080 cps-agent -enroll <token> -id pc7 -site wh1` (Windows: add `-install` for a service, or use `cps-agent-gui.exe`). ASUS routers: koolshare plugin or the `/jffs` package (see INSTALL.md §5).

Checks: `cpsctl status`, `cpsctl printers` (each printer, usable or why not), `cpsctl diag <printer_id>`, `cpsctl test <printer_id>`.

## 9. Testing without hardware

```bash
go run ./vprint/cmd/vprint -count 2 -id wh1-pack -render -render-dir /tmp/labels   # printers on :19100+, gallery on :19200
cp server/config.example.json config.json && go run ./server/cmd/cps -config config.json
```

The example config points `sim-pack-01` at the virtual printer. Fault injection: `POST http://localhost:19200/control` with `{"state":"media_out"}`, `{"offline":true}`, `{"close_on_print":true}`, `{"state":"always_printing"}` (jobs end `sent_unknown`).
